original_question: Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups.
target_in_paper: The second half of the final open question in Section 4: "What is the Frobenius variety generated only by the symmetric ones? and by the pseudo-symmetric ones?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct open problem and stays in the right part of the paper: it asks about the Frobenius variety generated by the pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups, exactly the pseudo-symmetric half of the paper’s final question in Section 4. It also correctly uses the paper’s own language of a Frobenius variety and of a family being generated.
missing_details: State that the ambient objects are numerical semigroups, i.e. cofinite additive submonoids of N, where N is the set of nonnegative integers.
Define the Frobenius number F(S) of a numerical semigroup S as the greatest integer not belonging to S.
Define pseudo-symmetric precisely: S is pseudo-symmetric if F(S) is even and for every x not in S, either F(S)-x belongs to S or x=F(S)/2.
Define a Frobenius variety V as a nonempty family of numerical semigroups such that: if S,T are in V, then S∩T is in V; and if S is in V with S≠N, then S∪{F(S)} is in V.
Clarify that "generated by" means the least Frobenius variety containing all pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups, equivalently the intersection of all Frobenius varieties containing that class.

To stay maximally faithful to the paper’s phrasing, note that this is the pseudo-symmetric half of a paired question about the symmetric and pseudo-symmetric subclasses, posed right after observing that irreducible numerical semigroups generate the whole class of numerical semigroups.
No ambient ring/field, characteristic, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency assumptions are part of this problem; the missing data are entirely semigroup-theoretic definitions.
refined_question: Let PS be the class of all pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups S⊆N, where a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of N, F(S) denotes the Frobenius number of S, and pseudo-symmetric means that F(S) is even and, for every x∉S, either F(S)-x∈S or x=F(S)/2. Determine the Frobenius variety generated by PS; equivalently, determine the least nonempty family V of numerical semigroups containing every S in PS such that (i) if S,T∈V, then S∩T∈V, and (ii) if S∈V and S≠N, then S∪{F(S)}∈V.
equivalent_formulation: Describe the least Frobenius variety containing the class of all pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups.
justification: This is the paper-faithful sharpening of the draft because Section 4 explicitly asks, at the very end of the discussion of Frobenius varieties, for the Frobenius variety generated by the pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups. The nearby context needed to make the question stand alone comes from Section 3, where pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups are defined, and from Section 4, where both Frobenius varieties and the Frobenius variety generated by a family are defined. The immediately preceding sentence in Section 4 also explains the scope: although irreducible numerical semigroups generate all numerical semigroups as a Frobenius variety, the authors then ask separately about the symmetric subclass and the pseudo-symmetric subclass.
